'''Claudio Bunster Weitzman''' ({{IPA|es-419|ˈklawðjo ˈβunsteɾ|lang}}; born April 15, 1947) is a [[Chile]]an theoretical physicist. Until 2005 his name was '''Claudio Teitelboim Weitzman'''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Conmovedor fin de un secreto que duró 58 años | url=http://www.australvaldivia.cl/prontus4_nots/site/artic/20050905/pags/20050905013121.html | date = 2005-09-05 | accessdate=2015-11-22}}</ref>

==Biography==
Until 2005 Bunster thought he was the biological son of [[Volodia Teitelboim]], when he learned that his biological father was lawyer Bruno Bunster. He was convinced that this was a machination of the leadership of the Communist Party. He became estranged from his adoptive father, changed his name and did not attend his funeral.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cooperativa.cl |title=Volodia Teitelboim se confesó "triste" y "resignado" por la postura de Claudio Bunster |url=https://www.cooperativa.cl/noticias/cultura/literatura/volodia-teitelboim/volodia-teitelboim-se-confeso-triste-y-resignado-por-la-postura-de/2005-10-24/235242.html |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Cooperativa.cl |language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=S.A.P |first=El Mercurio |date=2008-02-01 |title=Claudio Bunster no asistirá a funeral de Volodia Teitelboim |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/nacional/2008/02/01/290989/claudio-bunster-no-asistira-a-funeral-de-volodia-teitelboim.html |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Emol |language=Spanish}}</ref> 

Claudio Bunster attended at [[Instituto Nacional General José Miguel Carrera]], a prestigious public high school of Santiago. Bunster was educated at the [[University of Chile]] and [[Princeton University]], where he earned his doctorate in physics in 1973. Bunster has conducted frontier research and taught at [[Princeton University]] and at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. He has also been "Long Term Member" of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at Princeton.

Bunster has been Director of the [[Centro de Estudios Científicos|Center for Scientific Studies]] (CECS<ref>[http://cecs.cl/website/index.php/en CECs]</ref>) from its inception in 1984. Originally operating from [[Santiago]], in 2000 this autonomous institute moved South of [[Chile]], [[Valdivia]], in the 40S parallel, where the search has expanded and deepened in the areas of life, our planet and the cosmos.

In addition to his research in theoretical physics and his work as Director of CECs, Bunster has engaged in public service. He was Scientific Adviser to the President during the administration of President [[Eduardo Frei Ruiz-Tagle]] (1994–2000). During his tenure as presidential adviser the Presidential Chairs in Science and the [[Millennium Science Initiative]] were established. He was also a member of the Panel on [[Human Rights]], established by the government, and involving both the civilian and the military, to address outstanding human rights issues.

Bunster has been especially involved in incorporating the armed forces in scientific endeavors, as a way of strengthening democracy through science. This interest has led to joint work in science among CECs, the [[Chilean Army|Army]], [[Chilean Navy|Navy]] and [[Chilean Air Force|Air Force]] of Chile and distinguished foreign institutions. Among the fruits of these collaborations are several unprecedented expeditions to [[Antarctica]] in which Bunster was directly involved.

He received Chile's [[National Prize for Exact Sciences (Chile)|National Prize for Exact Sciences]] in 1995<ref>[http://www.uchile.cl/portal/presentacion/historia/grandes-figuras/premios-nacionales/ciencias-/6568/claudio-teitelboim-weitzmann National Prize of Sciences of Chile]</ref> and was elected to the Academy of Sciences of the United States in 2005<ref>[http://www.pnas.org/content/105/27/9137 Academy of Sciences of the United States]</ref> and was made Honorary Member of the Solvay Institutes in Brussels in 2007.<ref>[http://www.solvayinstitutes.be/index.php?pageid=1&ssid=2&sssid=6 Honorary Members of the Solvay Institutes] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131217221437/http://www.solvayinstitutes.be/index.php?pageid=1&ssid=2&sssid=6 |date=2013-12-17 }}</ref> [[The World Academy of Sciences]] for the advancement of science in developing countries, awarded Bunster in 2013, with the TWAS-Lenovo Prize.<ref>[http://twas.ictp.it/news-in-home-page/news/chilean-physicist-wins-twas-lenovo-prize TWAS-Lenovo Prize] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131012020936/http://twas.ictp.it/news-in-home-page/news/chilean-physicist-wins-twas-lenovo-prize |date=2013-10-12 }}</ref>
